problem.text: Real numbers $x$ and $y$ are chosen independently and uniformly at random from the interval $[0,1]$. Which of the following numbers is closest to the probability that $x$, $y$, and $1$ are the side lengths of an obtuse triangle?

steps.title: Where to start: probability as area
steps.body: Picking $x$ and $y$ independently and uniformly from $[0,1]$ is the same as picking a random point $(x,y)$ in the unit square. The square has area $1$, so the probability of any condition is the area of the region where it holds. So the job is to turn "obtuse triangle" into conditions on $x$ and $y$ and draw them.

your_turn.prompt: Since $x\le1$ and $y\le1$, which of the three sides $x$, $y$, $1$ is the longest?

steps.title: Condition 1: a triangle exists
steps.body: Three lengths make a triangle when each one is less than the sum of the other two. With sides $x$, $y$, $1$, two of these checks are automatic, because $1$ is at least as long as $x$ and $y$. Careful: the remaining check really matters, and forgetting it is a common mistake.

your_turn.prompt: Which triangle inequality is not automatic? Where is it true in the square?
your_turn.answer: $x+y>1$: the part of the square above the line $x+y=1$.

steps.title: Condition 2: the triangle is obtuse
steps.body: The largest angle is across from the longest side, which is $1$. By the converse of the Pythagorean theorem, that angle is more than $90^\circ$ exactly when the squares of the two shorter sides add up to less than the square of the longest side. Careful: the other direction, $x^2+y^2>1$, means the triangle is acute.

your_turn.prompt: Write the obtuse condition as an inequality, and describe the region in the square where it holds.
your_turn.answer: $x^2+y^2<1$: the points inside the quarter circle of radius $1$ centered at $(0,0)$.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body:
We need both: inside the quarter circle and above the line $x+y=1$. The line cuts the quarter circle at $(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$, so the region is the quarter disk (area $\frac{\pi}{4}$) minus the triangle with vertices $(0,0)$, $(1,0)$, $(0,1)$ (area $\frac12$):
$$\frac{\pi}{4}-\frac12\approx0.785-0.5=0.285.$$
The closest choice is $0.29$. The answer is **(C)**.

wrong_choices.E: $0.79\approx\frac{\pi}{4}$ is the whole quarter circle. It forgets the triangle condition $x+y>1$; points below that line do not make a triangle at all.
wrong_choices.D: $0.50$ is the probability that the three lengths make a triangle at all (above $x+y=1$). The question also asks for the triangle to be obtuse.
wrong_choices.A: $0.21\approx1-\frac{\pi}{4}$ uses $x^2+y^2>1$, which is the acute condition. Obtuse means the two short sides squared add to less than $1$.
